Use case: ads-marketing. Create ONE finished premium academic public-awareness social-media poster, square 1:1, ideally 1536x1536. Full-bleed warm ivory paper, near-black typography, vermilion red and restrained teal accents. Swiss editorial design meets sophisticated conceptual cut-paper illustration, crisp flat print shapes with subtle paper grain. Strong asymmetrical grid, generous whitespace, very large headline, body readable on phone. No rounded dashboard UI, no stock robot heads, no neon, no gradients, no fake logos. All text exactly as specified; don't add invented claims. Margin 7%. Source footer clear and legible. This is a three-card campaign on LLM social simulation accountability.
Card 01 / 03: concept and stakes. Top small eyebrow "SIMULATION AS ALIBI  /  AIES 2026". Huge headline over 3 short lines: "AI simulates society.\nWho wrote\nthe rules?"
Central conceptual editorial illustration: an elegant isometric miniature society of small human paper silhouettes connected by teal lines, standing on an ivory platform. One corner is visibly peeled back, revealing red rule-setting tracks and a human hand placing the underlying architecture. The image illustrates human authorship, not puppets or mind control. Include a small printed tag "“Emergence”" next to the visible agent layer and "Design choices" next to the revealed layer.
Below illustration, body "When simulation outputs inform real decisions, hidden design choices can escape scrutiny."
Three concise separated labels: "Knowledge laundered" / "Responsibility displaced" / "Legitimacy extracted".
Small readable qualification: "Emergence can be real. Its conditions are still designed."
Footer: "Tang & Lin · Simulation as Alibi · 01 / 03" and "github.com/JamieJustTang/simulation-as-alibi".
Do not use literal backslash-n: line breaks are layout instructions.

Card 02 / 03: precise evidence poster. Eyebrow "THE EVIDENCE  /  142-PAPER AUDIT". Large title "Who disappears\nfrom the explanation?"
Very large vermilion "14 / 17", with clear prominent explanatory text "papers with absent designer attribution\nmake the strongest emergence claims."
Smaller line "82% of the absent-attribution group — not 82% of all papers."
Below, create three clean horizontal proportional bars sharing one scale, title "Absent designer attribution, by emergence intensity". Bar labels and exact end labels: "Low" = "2/36 · 5.6%"; "Medium" = "1/49 · 2.0%"; "High" = "14/57 · 24.6%". High bar red, other bars muted teal. Ensure bar lengths accurately proportional to 5.6, 2.0, 24.6; no fake data or icon counts. This is a careful statistical chart with spacious label alignment.
Under chart, "Attribution is assessed in the sentence explaining why emergence occurs."
Bottom note in legible type: "Single-coder corpus; approximately 80% preprints. Association does not establish causation."
Footer "Tang & Lin · Simulation as Alibi · Table 2 · 02 / 03" and "github.com/JamieJustTang/simulation-as-alibi".
Use real line breaks instead of literal slash sequences.
